response.title: which power station is safest to keep inside an apartment
response.answer:
For keeping a portable power station inside an apartment, my top recommendation is a LiFePO₄ (lithium iron phosphate, or LFP) battery power station with independently certified electrical safety.

LFP batteries are generally more thermally stable and less prone to thermal runaway than conventional lithium-ion chemistries such as NMC. However, no large battery is completely fireproof.

What makes a power station safe indoors?

I would prioritize these features, in order:

UL 2743 certification — a key safety standard for portable power packs. Look for certification of the complete unit, not just individual components.

LiFePO₄ battery chemistry — lower thermal-runaway risk than many other lithium-ion chemistries.

Battery management system (BMS) — protects against overheating, overcharging, overcurrent, and short circuits.

Good thermal management — temperature sensors, cooling, and automatic shutdown.

Manufacturer reliability — clear warranty, recall history, and accessible customer support.

For apartment use, I would also favor a smaller-capacity unit unless you genuinely need a large battery. Less stored energy generally means less potential energy released during a severe battery failure.

Three models worth considering

These are candidates to investigate, not a verified ranking of fire safety. I couldn't establish that one has a lower real-world fire risk than the others.

Shop

EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus

My pick for small apartment backup

Approximately 286 Wh, LFP battery. Suitable for laptops, routers, lights, and charging devices.

Compact capacity makes it appealing when you don't need to run large appliances.

Anker SOLIX C800X 1200 -Watts Portable Power Station

768 Wh, LFP battery. A middle-ground option for longer backup time.

Listed at $499.00

Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 Portable Power Station | 1,070Wh Li…

1,070 Wh, LFP battery. Better suited to extended outage backup, but stores considerably more energy.

Listed at $559.00

Before buying any of these, I would verify the exact model's UL 2743 listing through the certifying laboratory. UL confirms that UL 2743 addresses portable power packs; it is not equivalent to UL 9540 certification for permanently installed residential energy storage. 
UL Solutions
+1

Where to keep it in an apartment

On a stable, hard, nonflammable surface.

Away from curtains, bedding, heaters, and direct sunlight.

With ventilation clearance specified by the manufacturer.

Away from doorways and escape routes.

Preferably outside the bedroom.

Charge using the manufacturer's approved equipment, and avoid leaving it charging unattended or while sleeping.

One question that would change my recommendation: Are you planning to keep the power station plugged in 24/7 as a UPS, or store it charged for occasional power outages?

Those are different safety situations, and I would choose differently depending on your answer.
